angle: The bottleneck is organizational adoption, not code generation speed.
sourceTitle: AI Is Producing More Software. Why Isn’t It Being Used?
linkedinPost:
AI can help teams ship more software. So why doesn’t customer value go up in lockstep?

Wharton’s new study says the gains stall in human bottlenecks—product definition, user onboarding, compliance reviews, change management. As someone who ships AI into customer-facing operations, I can confirm: output isn’t impact.

In the field, I see the same pattern:
- A backlog factory generates features; no one measures adoption after release.
- Legal and risk enter late, forcing months of rework.
- Training plans assume people have time they don’t.

My playbook that actually moves the needle:
- Define “adopted” up front (e.g., 60% of agents using the AI tool daily by week 4) and instrument it.
- Pull risk/compliance into sprint 0 with pre-approved patterns.
- Budget for change load: job aids, “brown-bag” sessions, floor support for two cycles.

AI accelerates building. Enterprises must accelerate validating, enabling, and owning the change.

Where does adoption die most often in your org: definition, governance, or enablement?
xPost: AI can flood you with features. Value shows up only when humans adopt. Define “adopted,” instrument it, pull risk in at sprint 0, and budget real change load. Output ≠ impact. #AIAdoption #EnterpriseAI
